summary: Landable. DELTA VERIFIED BY CONSTRUCTION: `git diff --cached -- . ':(exclude)baselines/review.txt' | sha256sum` returns 7cadde4311554511eb898e9b58c5e16654f73bfabd54740c1c9c31ee32580a56 exactly -- the core I passed at rounds 3 and 4 -- so all eight other staged paths are byte-identical and the whole round-5 delta is the rewritten `rounds:M0.79` line at baselines/review.txt:29. Still no test file in the staged set; the mutation surface remains the prose governing my own output, which did not move. THE CORRECTED ATTRIBUTION MATCHES THE ARTIFACTS, measured rather than accepted. Four recorded rounds, four staged_tree values, and exactly one carries the ADR: `git ls-tree -r --name-only` over 73bbbb561fe7 (r1), 469567ea8610 (r2), b18857410502 (r3) and 2cdc387d884f (r4) returns 622, 623, 622, 622 paths, and 0036-the-idempotency-key-... appears in 469567ea ALONE. So 'ONE sweep reached a reviewed hash' is exact, and both r2 verdicts are `changes-requested` with a blocking finding on that path from BOTH roles -- 'both roles blocked on it' is exact. 'Cost two rounds' holds: r3 (7cadde43) is two `pass` verdicts whose entire discharge text is the ADR's absence from the index. 'EXACTLY ONE REVIEWER CATCH IS RECORDED' is now correct where the round-4 draft was not: p079-r4.txt:113 carried 'swept ... into this commit TWICE' and 'Caught both times only because a reviewer diffed against the recorded staged_tree', and no second reviewer catch exists in .harness/review -- I grepped every M0.79 verdict and there are eight, four hashes times two roles, with one ADR finding pair. THE ORPHAN IS AS I IDENTIFIED IT AND AS THE LINE NOW STATES: .harness/review/77b8605b69d17e...gates exists with NO .reviewer.json and NO .test-reviewer.json beside it, written 07:19:34, thirteen seconds before 7cadde43's .gates at 07:19:47 and thirteen before p079-r3.txt at 07:19:47.176 -- so 'no packet or verdict exists for it' is checkable and true, and 'I caught it myself' is the only account consistent with a gates record that never became a review. One honest limit, stated because the line's own subject is inflated claims: 77b8605b is a diff hash, not a git object (`git cat-file -t` refuses it), and a .gates file records only pass/fail per script, so the artifacts show a sweep-shaped GAP at that point, not the ADR itself. The line does not claim otherwise -- it names the tree only for the sweep it can name (`469567ea8610`) and says 'at 77b8605b' for the one it cannot. That is the right asymmetry and I confirm it. COLLATERAL CLAIMS RE-MEASURED, not carried over: cost.md appears in the standards list of NONE of p079.txt, p079-r2, p079-r3, p079-r4 (all four select exactly git/sdd/testing/performance); its two hits in p079-r4 are inside the diff body being reviewed, not the selection. The ADR is 208 lines in 469567ea and names `CommitDelta` twice and `Checkpoint` six times, so the second production minor's fix -- 'both delta encodings' becoming '`CommitDelta` AND `Checkpoint`' -- is not just a wording change, it is true of the artifact, and it stops repeating the conflation the M4.10 entry two lines above records as its own round-2 defect ('`Checkpoint` is not a `ChainEntry`'). backlog.md:124 still marks M4.10b todo. check-reviewed.sh:195 keys the waiver on `rounds:M0.79`, which the added line uses. MY THREE MINORS FROM ROUNDS 3-4 STAND UNCHANGED and are carried below at the same locations, because the bytes they cite are provably the same bytes; that they are in the commit body I still cannot verify, as the body is not in the staged diff. ONE NEW MINOR ON THE ROUND-5 LINE ITSELF, which is the first production minor half-fixed: the entry's opening still asserts the impossibility its own later paragraph withdraws.

findings.summary: The fix for 'the entry claims splitting is impossible' was APPENDED as a correction rather than applied at the sentence that makes the claim, so one line now asserts both that no further split exists and that one does.
findings.failure_scenario: The opening reads 'Splitting further means committing a skill without the index row that resolves it, or an index row pointing at a file the commit does not carry' -- a universal claim that every further split orphans something. Roughly 2,300 characters later the same line reads 'A SPLIT SEAM DOES EXIST and an earlier draft denied it: skill plus adapter plus index rows is self-consistent, and the `review/SKILL.md` paragraph plus the two briefs is self-consistent once that lands.' The second is a counterexample to the first: the half it names carries the skill AND its generated index rows together, so it produces neither of the two orphans the opening enumerates. I verified the counterexample is real rather than rhetorical -- build-index.sh:32 globs `.agents/skills/*/` from the worktree, so a commit carrying brevity/SKILL.md plus the AGENTS.md and skills/README.md rows regenerates identically, and nothing in that set links to the two `.claude/agents/` briefs. The opening sentence is byte-identical to the round-4 draft at p079-r4.txt:113, so the round-5 edit added the retraction without removing what it retracts. Concrete cost: this file is what a future session reads to decide whether a round-budget override was honest. check-reviewed.sh:195 accepts ANY added `rounds:M0.79` line, so nothing downstream reconciles the two halves, and a reader who stops at the first sentence -- the position an argument's thesis normally occupies -- takes away exactly the claim the production reviewer asked to be removed. This is the failure mode the M0.76 entry three lines above and the M4.10 entry one line above both name in their own words: 'every fix added a REASON beside the correction' and 'deleted rather than rewritten', the second being the remedy. The strictly better edit is to cut the opening's second clause and let 'THIS COMMIT IS ALREADY THE SPLIT' carry the argument, which is the true and sufficient one -- the files arrived from outside a task and build-index blocked every commit until they landed. NOT BLOCKING, under review.md:45 minors-land: the true fact is present in the line, both halves are visible to anyone reading it end to end, and buying a sixth round for prose is precisely what the M0.76 entry records as its own defect.

findings.summary: Unchanged from rounds 3-4 and re-verified against these bytes: the provenance paragraph corrects the abbreviation claim thirty lines below it, under an unrelated heading, leaving the false sentence in place at the point of use.
findings.failure_scenario: Line 52 reads 'No invented abbreviations (cfg, impl, req, res, fn, auth). The tokenizer splits them the same as the full word: zero tokens saved'. Lines 81-85 say the opposite about the same example: '"auth" is one token where "authentication" is several, so that abbreviation does save tokens'. The correction sits under '## Write at full length when', two headings past '## Never fake-compress', so an agent that reads the Never-fake-compress section and applies it never reaches the contradiction. The file is loaded for output style, not read end to end. Carried forward unchanged so the landing hash carries it; recording rather than fixing remains my recommendation, since the fix surface is new prose in the file that governs reviewer output.

findings.summary: Unchanged and re-verified: the out-of-scope carve-out cites its own line number, the self-citation class the gate landed in 69b4f13 exists to refuse.
findings.failure_scenario: The carve-out points at 'line 43 of this file' for the Never-cut list. Any insertion above line 43 -- including the round-2 and round-3 edits that already moved text in this file -- silently retargets the citation at a different rule, and no gate reads prose line references. 69b4f13's commit subject is 'name the review rules, because a number names nothing and goes stale', and check-rule-citations.sh enforces that for review.md only, so this instance is outside its reach and will go stale unnoticed. The remedy is to name the heading rather than the line.

findings.summary: Unchanged and re-verified: the file demands provenance for a measured claim on line 43 while asserting three unmeasured tokenizer claims on lines 49-54.
findings.failure_scenario: Never-cut now protects 'the provenance of a claim -- measured, inferred, or not run', which was my round-1 T1 and is the right fix. Lines 49-54 then assert tokenizer behaviour in the present tense with no tokenizer named and no measurement cited. The rule and its violation are eleven lines apart in the file that governs how every reviewer states a claim, which is the weakest possible position from which to enforce non-negotiable 4. The three rules survive on readability alone, so this stays minor and unfixed is acceptable; a caveat naming the arithmetic as unmeasured would discharge it.
